entities.summary:
Felix of Valois, OSsT (French: Félix de Valois); was a French Catholic former Cistercian hermit and a co-founder of the Trinitarian Order.

Born around 1180 in Valois, France, Felix spent most of his life in solitude, reflecting on his spiritual journey.

In 1208, he co-founded the Trinitarian Order with two other Cistercian monks, Pierre de Marigny and Guy de Lusignan.

Felix's unique approach to spirituality emphasized the importance of prayer, contemplation, and service to others.

He spent the remainder of his life in various monasteries across France, establishing the Trinitarian Order and promoting his spiritual teachings.

Felix of Valois died on November 11, 1212, at the age of 32.

His legacy as a spiritual leader and founder of the Trinitarian Order has endured for centuries, inspiring many to pursue a life of prayer, service, and devotion.
